characters.name_or_role: Wife (left side of bed, brown sweater, hair bun) - SPEAKER_01
personality_traits: Nostalgic/wistful — opens the skit musing about a past social norm ('remember when you used to excuse yourself to fart?'), positioning her as the one who notices and comments on changed behavior
Passive-aggressive commentator — delivers her line as an observation/needle rather than a direct confrontation, eyes cutting sideways at her husband instead of addressing him head-on
Physically withdrawn/guarded — stays curled toward her own phone with elbows tucked in, body angled slightly away from her husband despite being inches apart
emotional_range: Detached mild irritation (scrolling, blank stare) at the open
Building disbelief / bug-eyed alarm as she delivers the line
Faint, tight-lipped smugness/self-satisfaction by the final frame, as if she landed the jab
expressions: 0:00 neutral, half-lidded, screen-lit stare down at phone
0:02-0:03 eyes widen sharply, eyebrows raise, mouth drops open into a slightly gaping 'o' as she starts speaking ('Remember when...')
0:04 eyes remain saucer-wide and fixed sideways on her husband, mouth still parted mid-sentence ('...to fart?')
0:07-0:08 (after husband's rebuttal) gaze softens, mouth closes into a small closed-lip smirk, eyebrows settle — a quiet 'I made my point' look
gestures: Holds phone low and close to her chest with both hands throughout, thumbs poised but still
Head/eyes swivel toward her husband without turning her torso, signaling she's talking at him rather than to him
No hand gestures accompany the line — all emphasis is carried in the face, consistent with a stop-motion puppet's limited rig but used for comic timing
characters.interactions_notes: She initiates the exchange unprompted, breaking the shared silence of two people lying in bed each absorbed in a separate screen. She looks at him; he does not look back at her, keeping his eyes on his own phone even while responding — an asymmetric eye-contact dynamic that visually reinforces the joke (two people 'together' but each in their own device-lit bubble). Her tone/expression suggests she believes she's won the exchange by the end, while he seems mildly stung by the accusation embedded in her nostalgia.

characters.name_or_role: Husband (right side of bed, glasses, sweater vest, headphones/wires) - SPEAKER_00
personality_traits: Deflective/defensive — his rebuttal ('That man was trying to get married') reframes past-tense fart etiquette as strategic performance rather than genuine courtesy, dodging the implication that he's grown lazier or less considerate
Withdrawn/absorbed — remains visually locked onto his own phone through the entire scene, barely reacting physically even while delivering a comeback line
Dry, deadpan comic timing — the joke lands because his face barely moves; the humor is entirely in the contrast between his flat delivery and the sharpness of the retort
emotional_range: Flat, sedated boredom/indifference for most of the clip (heavy-lidded eyes, downturned mouth)
A flicker of defensiveness/irritation as he answers back, mouth opening into a slight grimace
Returns to flat indifference immediately after, unaffected
expressions: 0:00-0:04 static droopy-eyed, mouth curved slightly down in a neutral frown, glasses reflecting phone glow — completely unreactive to his wife's opening line
0:05-0:06 eyebrows tick up slightly and mouth opens into a small downturned oval as he delivers 'That man was trying to get married' — the closest he comes to an active expression in the clip
0:07+ face resets to the same flat, glazed, screen-fixed look as the opening
gestures: Holds phone up higher and closer to his face than his wife, two-handed grip, elbows resting on wrapped/bandaged-looking forearms (visual gag suggesting overuse of the phone/devices)
Head stays facing forward toward his own screen throughout — never turns toward his wife, even to respond
No other body movement; torso and shoulders remain static against the pillow the entire scene
characters.interactions_notes: He answers her verbally but not physically — same power dynamic as her: both are technically 'in dialogue' but neither breaks visual attention from their own phone, which is the visual thesis of the whole skit (title 'Low Battery People' implies emotionally/attentionally depleted couple). His deadpan non-reaction to being needled, followed by a quick verbal jab back, suggests a long-married couple's practiced, low-effort bickering rather than real conflict — no anger, no raised voices, just mutual screen-numbed sniping.
